question_text: A 67-year-old man presents to his primary care physician complaining of frequent urination overnight. He states that for several years he has had trouble maintaining his urine stream along with the need for frequent urination, but the nighttime urination has only recently started. The patient also states that he has had 2 urinary tract infections in the last year, which he had never had previously. On exam, his temperature is 98.8°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 124/68 mmHg, pulse is 58/min, and respirations are 13/min. On digital rectal exam, the prostate is enlarged but feels symmetric and smooth. Which of the following is a possible consequence of this condition?

                    ### Question
                    A 67-year-old man presents to his primary care physician complaining of frequent urination overnight. He states that for several years he has had trouble maintaining his urine stream along with the need for frequent urination, but the nighttime urination has only recently started. The patient also states that he has had 2 urinary tract infections in the last year, which he had never had previously. On exam, his temperature is 98.8°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 124/68 mmHg, pulse is 58/min, and respirations are 13/min. On digital rectal exam, the prostate is enlarged but feels symmetric and smooth. Which of the following is a possible consequence of this condition?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Increased serum AFP
opb. Increased serum ALP
opc. Increased serum creatinine
opd. Increased serum hCG
ope. Malignant transformation

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
An enlarged prostate can lead to urinary retention, obstructed urine flow, increased residual urine volume, and urinary stasis, all of which increase the risk of urinary tract infections. Urinary obstruction can also lead to obstructive nephropathy, potentially increasing serum creatinine levels. Therefore, increased serum creatinine is a possible consequence of this condition.
